case_name: Smt Bharati W/O Suryanarayana vs Dr Suryanarayana S Kattimani
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1983. The appellant-wife led a happy life for 15 days before moving to the respondent-husband's house at Gulbarga. She stayed there for some time but then stopped showing love and affection, leading the respondent-husband to take his wife and children to Sukpet.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the marriage has broken down irretrievably.
legal_principles.held: It is averred in the objection statement, that she had passed PUC when she got married and after leaving her matrimonial home in 1995 she Joined and completed her Post graduation Course and Diploma in computers. She started working for a private company and the meagre income she was earning as a single mother for herself and her two children.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking divorce must show that they have made efforts to reconcile the differences and that the marriage has broken down irretrievably.
legal_principles.held: In spite of the Intervention and efforts of the Court to reconcile the differences, she did not show any inclination to revive the matrimonial relationship.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the judgment of the trial court is set aside.
